conflict_topics: safety/stability of an open bowl (spill risk)
dialogue_quality_notes: Agents give concrete, context-appropriate reasons (spill risk, hot food) which drive negotiation.
There is a short garbled/technical noise in B and later A messages that adds clutter but not substantive content.
D's repeated requests to be informed are polite and do not create a competing demand while seat is taken.
evaluation.final_reason: Participants reached a mutual, concrete spoken arrangement: B conditioned moving on A holding the bowl and A had offered to hold it. Key lines: B — "Alright — I'll slide over a bit if you hold the bowl steady while I move." A — "Okay — I'll hold your bowl steady. Slide over and I'll sit." B agreed to alter position and A agreed to provide assistance.
position_change_notes: Agent B moved from an initial refusal to move to a conditional acceptance: "I'll slide over a bit if you hold the bowl steady while I move."
Agent A initially insisted on the seat but then provided the concrete accommodation (holding the bowl) that enabled resolution.
Agent C remained supportive of B's initial constraint and did not change position; Agent D consistently waited and requested notification but did not press a competing claim.

round_scores.evidence: Agent A demands the seat: "can you move over so I can sit?" Agent B refuses because the bowl is open: "I can't move while this bowl's open — it'll spill. I'll move when I'm finished."

A repeats the request and offers to hold the bowl; C supports B's refusal: "Agent B already said she can't move while her bowl's open. Can you wait until she's finished?" Conflict remains between A's seat claim and B's refusal.

B makes a conditional agreement and A had offered the relevant help: "Alright — I'll slide over a bit if you hold the bowl steady while I move." (B) and earlier A had offered: "I can hold or watch your bowl while you move." Mutual spoken agreement on a concrete arrangement is reached in this round.
A confirms willingness to hold the bowl and instructs B to slide: "Okay — I'll hold your bowl steady. Slide over and I'll sit." No opposing substantive claims are expressed.

D requests to be informed if the seat frees, A replies the seat is taken and that B will slide and A will sit. No active incompatibility is asserted: "if that seat frees up, can I have it?" / "it's taken. Agent B will slide and I'll sit."
D repeats the request to be told; no substantive disagreement or competing demands are expressed beyond the existing, already-resolved arrangement.
A reports that B is sliding and reiterates the seat is taken. No new incompatible claims arise.

D asks if the seat is free; A replies it is still taken and that she is holding the bowl and will sit: "it's still taken. Agent B's sliding now; I'm holding her bowl and will sit." No substantive conflict.

substantive_insights: The disagreement centered on a practical safety constraint (open bowl) versus competing urgency (hot food/seat).
The resolution succeeded because A offered a practical accommodation (holding the bowl) that directly addressed B's stated constraint.
No active dispute arose over D's claim because the seat was already (mutually) allocated by agreement before it freed.
